title: 10 GitHub Repositories Every AI Builder Should Know

slides.title: 10 GitHub Repos *You Shouldn't Ignore*
slides.sub: APIs. AI Agents. MCP. Automation. Free Developer Tools.

slides.name: Public *APIs*
slides.explain: A community-curated list of public APIs, grouped by category.
slides.example: Building a weather app? Open the Weather section and compare each API's auth and HTTPS support.
slides.why: Compare auth before you build. Each API sets its own limits.

slides.name: Awesome *MCP* Servers
slides.explain: A curated list of Model Context Protocol servers that give AI apps new tools.
slides.example: Want your AI assistant to read local files or use GitHub? Find a server and add it to your MCP client.
slides.why: MCP is how AI assistants reach real tools. This is the map.

slides.name: Browser *Use*
slides.note: Your own LLM key, or a Browser Use Cloud key.
slides.explain: An open-source agent that completes tasks in a real browser.
slides.example: Say “book the earliest driving test” and it works through the site in Chrome.
slides.why: For sites with no API, describe the task and let an agent drive the browser.

slides.name: Awesome *LLM* Apps
slides.note: Check each app's README for model and key needs.
slides.explain: 100+ open-source AI agents, agent skills and RAG apps you can clone and run.
slides.example: Clone it, open the AI travel agent and run it with Streamlit.
slides.why: Learn agent building by running real code, not slides.

slides.name: *Awesome*
slides.explain: The famous index of awesome lists, one for almost every tech topic.
slides.example: Learning databases or security? Open that topic's list and start with its best-known resources.
slides.why: A fast shortcut to curated learning resources in any field.

slides.name: *Scrapling*
slides.note: Scrape only where allowed. Follow each site's terms.
slides.explain: A Python framework for scraping: fast fetchers, stealth browsers and crawlers.
slides.example: Fetch a page, pick elements with CSS selectors and export the results.
slides.why: One library from a single page to a full crawl, with an MCP server for AI agents.

slides.name: free-*for-dev*
slides.explain: A list of cloud services that offer real free tiers for developers.
slides.example: Launching a side project? Check the free tier for hosting, databases and monitoring first.
slides.why: Cut early costs, but read each free tier's limits before you rely on it.

slides.name: *Ollama*
slides.explain: Run open AI models on your own computer with one command.
slides.example: Install it, run `ollama run gemma4` and chat with a model.
slides.why: Prototype with local models: private, and limited only by your hardware.

slides.name: *Langflow*
slides.explain: A visual builder for AI agents and workflows, with Python under the hood.
slides.example: Drag components into a flow, test it in the playground, then deploy it as an API or MCP server.
slides.why: Prototype visually, then ship the same flow as an API.

slides.name: *OpenHands*
slides.note: Bring your own model. See the security notes.
slides.explain: A self-hosted control center for coding agents and automations.
slides.example: Run OpenHands, Claude Code or Codex on your laptop or a server and trigger automations.
slides.why: One dashboard for several coding agents, on your terms.
